text:
leo_sales: BankCo POC kickoff tomorrow. They want a single-line explainer on BYOK vs HSM, plus a short security Q&A and a rough HSM premium for the POC. Need this in 30m.

sara_ps: quick context: theyre in finance, must pass internal audit. Likely need FIPS/HSM attestation but may accept cloud-HSM with evidence.

neha_sec: short single-line: "We support cloud KMS (CMEK) with envelope encryption for hosted flows and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments; HSM provides hardware FIPS attestation and stronger key isolation."

leo_sales: perfect. Now Q&A they asked to pre-fill in the questionnaire - can someone drop concise answers?

ben_se: dropping quick answers (feel free to trim):
Q: Where are keys stored?
A: For CMEK: keys remain in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS). We use envelope encryption: we receive only wrapped data keys and ciphertext; plaintext keys are never stored. For HSM: keys are on the HSM and never exported.

Q: Do keys leave your environment?
A: No. With CMEK our services receive only wrapped DEKs (data encryption keys) from your KMS and perform decryption operations via the normal KMS APIs or client-side unwrap depending on deployment. For Private/HSM the key material does not leave the module.

Q: Rotation / rekey?
A: Rotation schedule is customer-configurable. Recommended: 90-day rotation for high-sensitivity workloads; 365 days typical. We support key versioning and automated re-wrapping jobs during rotation windows.

Q: Auditability / logs?
A: Customer must enable KMS audit logs (CloudTrail / Cloud Audit Logs) and provide read access or periodic exports. We also emit event telemetry for envelope operations to your audit sink when configured.

ben_se: config snippet (CMEK hosted):
```bash
# set the KMS key we will use to wrap model artifact keys
export REDWOOD_CMEK_KEY_ARN=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:222222222222:key/abcd-1234-ef56
# grant Redwood service principal kms:GenerateDataKey,kms:Decrypt
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/pocexample --policy file://redwood-trust-policy.json
```

neha_sec: compliance notes (concise):
- If you require attested HSM (FIPS 140-2/140-3) provide required certificate/serial numbers and desired assurance level.
- If policy prohibits cross-account decrypt, mention whether you will create a Redwoood-grantee service account or allow our principal.
- For strict non-export requirements, Private deployment with on-prem HSM is the pattern.

infra-eng: logistics/time: cloud CMEK POC setup: ~1-3 business days after we get key ARN + IAM grant. Cloud-HSM attestation flow: ~3-7 business days. Dedicated or on-prem HSM provisioning with physical module: 10+ business days (hardware & legal).

leo_sales: ballpark HSM premium ask? they want a number to budget against now.

neha_sec: ballpark for short POC: cloud-KMS (CMEK) = no extra Redwood key premium (standard hosted usage applies). Cloud-HSM attestation + Dedicated slot = approx +$6k/mo for a small reserved HSM add-on for POC. On-prem physical HSM and long-term reservation materially higher (custom). This is a placeholder; legal/pricing will follow a line-item quote.

leo_sales: good. One-line summary for email + attached mini-QA: can someone produce a 2-sentence line?

sara_ps: two-sentence: "We support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS (CMEK) for hosted flows and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments. For the POC we recommend CMEK if youre okay with cloud KMS envelope flows; if you require FIPS-attested HSM we can do Dedicated or Private with an HSM add-on (ballpark +$6k/mo for a POC)."

leo_sales: sending now. cc: security questionnaire.

deploy-bot: POC project created: POC-1987. Questionnaire attached and owner set to leo_sales.

infra-eng: next steps if they confirm HSM: open ticket with VPC peer details, target ASN, and whether they want cross-account KMS grants or a delegated grantee account.

neha_sec: also request from BankCo: preferred rotation cadence, KMS key ARN(s), audit log bucket or log export location, and HSM attestation docs (if applicable).

leo_sales: noted. closing thread once they reply. Thanks all.
